newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN CENTRAL BANK ISSUES REVISABLE RATE CD'S.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN CENTRAL BANK ISSUES REVISABLE RATE CD'S.

text.p: The Belgian central bank has made an agreement with Belgium's 15 primary dealers in state debt that they will subscribe to certificates of deposit worth a total of 230 billion francs, the bank said on Monday.

It said in a statement that the issue would expire on December 31, 1998, the day before the transfer to European Economic and Monetary Union. Half of the paper, worth 115 billion francs, will have an interest rate revisable every two months. The other half will have a rate revisable every four months.

The bank said the operations would be spread over a three-week period starting today. A bank spokesman told Reuters that the interest rates of the revisable rate paper would be in line with market rates on Treasury bills.
The bank said the operation would have no influence on its foreign currency reserves nor on money market liquidity.

The operation is the result of a Belgian government plan to reduce Belgium's foreign debt by using captital gains on central bank gold sales of the past years to pay back foreign-currency denominated state debt.
The bank said that in its balance sheet -- which is reported every week -- the "unavailable reserve of capital gains on gold" entry will gradually be replace by a new entry: "bank certificates".
Traders said earlier this month the unusual issue was a way for the central bank to sterilise the impact on the money market of the debt buyback operation.
If the bank would have simply transferred the money to the Treasury, which then put it into the banking system, the impact on the money market would be huge.
